body:
Wago's specialized integer-sum emitter already uses four elements and four independent accumulators. This draft tests whether larger groups improve execution without excessive compilation, allocation or native-code costs. Normal Wago with its existing 4/4 optimization is the primary baseline throughout.

**Recommendation: investigate further with plain 16/4 and bounded code-buffer reservation.** The reservation restores the baseline compilation allocation count while keeping the same 16/4 native instructions. Reject the paired tail as the next optimization to adopt: its small direct gains do not repeat. No candidate has verified real-application gains, and short-loop and adjacent-control losses remain. Keep production 4/4 and leave this PR draft.

## Configurations and decisions

All configurations are private opt-in experiments under `wago_sumunroll`. Normal builds retain the original emitter; no new public option or environment lookup is added to normal compilation. H/T/P operate after Wago's existing first-iteration peel. Thresholds select the remaining count, not the original input count.

| Candidate | Group / accumulators | Additional behavior | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline | 4 / 4 | Existing specialized emitter | Production reference |
| A | 8 / 4 | Scalar remainder | Useful gains; not preferred over D |
| B | 8 / 8 | Four additional chains | No consistent benefit over A; more register demand |
| C | 2 / 2 | Exploratory smaller group | Reject: large execution losses |
| D | 16 / 4 | Scalar remainder | Simplest main-loop candidate |
| E | 16 / 8 | Four additional chains | No consistent benefit over D; more register demand |
| H | 16 / 4 | Four-element tail using the same chains, then scalar | Useful middle/cache gains; does not dominate D |
| T64 | 16 / 4 or 4 / 4 | Runtime gate at 64 remaining elements | Retain evidence; no real-workload case for promotion |
| T128 / T256 | 16 / 4 or 4 / 4 | Runtime gates at 128 / 256 remaining elements | Discovery only; no separate repeat |
| P | 16 / 4 | Two-load remainder using existing chains | Reject added tail complexity |
| DR | 16 / 4 | Bounded code-buffer reservation; unchanged D instructions | Best allocation mitigation; investigate further |
| PR | 16 / 4 | P plus reservation | Correctness tested; not timed because P fails the benefit rule |

The source Wasm, bounds proof, first-iteration peel, memory32 wrapping, trap behavior/metadata, memory effects, exit locals, zero-count handling and fallback paths are preserved. Register admission uses bounded storage and free registers; it does not introduce spills to admit a candidate. Failed register or code-budget admission selects existing 4/4 before mutation. No SSA, new IR, general loop rewrite, SIMD path or ARM64 emitter change is included.

For original count 512, the peel leaves 511 elements. D emits 496 grouped loads plus 15 scalar; H emits 496 +12 grouped +3 scalar. P keeps the same 496-element main work, then pairs the 15 remaining loads. The paired tail keeps separate 32-bit address/count updates and displacement-zero loads to preserve wrapping.

## Primary public `memory.sum` results

The unchanged corpus sum uses 512 elements and its existing input/oracle. It is a synthetic kernel, not an application-level gain. `CompileFull` includes decode, validation, compilation and close. Execution excludes compilation/setup. Lifecycle includes public compilation, instantiation, one call and close.

Each arrow shows that row's own normal-Wago baseline → candidate median. Baselines vary between interleaved sets; these are not simultaneous head-to-head rankings across phases. Negative deltas mean faster. `*` means benchstat p<.05, without multiple-comparison adjustment; `p=0.000` means p<.001. A nonsignificant result does not prove equivalence.

| Set | Execution ns | Execution Δ | Public compile µs | Compile Δ | Compile B / objects | Lifecycle µs | Lifecycle Δ |

| T64 first | 98.225 → 87.215 | -11.21%* | 22.6660 → 23.8780 | +5.35%* | 23361/108 → 25153/110 | 55.1430 → 56.0985 | +1.73%* |
| T64 repeat | 99.615 → 87.810 | -11.85%* | 24.9040 → 27.0745 | +8.72%* | 23360/108 → 25153/110 | 62.0545 → 64.1975 | +3.45%* |
| P, cost qualification only | 96.490 → 90.640 | -6.06%* | 22.9845 → 22.9755 | -0.04% | 23360/108 → 25153/110 | 56.9025 → 56.5990 | -0.53% |
| DR first | 97.435 → 88.110 | -9.57%* | 23.1505 → 23.1510 | +0.00% | 23361/108 → 23617/108 | 56.6440 → 56.8150 | +0.30% |
| DR repeat | 97.070 → 87.250 | -10.12%* | 22.9805 → 23.2855 | +1.33%* | 23361/108 → 23617/108 | 55.3665 → 55.6240 | +0.47% |

Execution allocates **0 B / 0 objects** in every measured execution row. D/H/T64/P public compilation has 110 allocation objects versus 108 for normal 4/4, and roughly 1792–1793 extra bytes. The corresponding lifecycle is 26737 B /119 objects versus 24945 B /117. The execution gain therefore does not imply a faster compile-and-run-once workload.

DR's normal comparisons use 23617 B /108 objects versus 23361 B /108: **+256 B (+1.10%) and no extra allocation object**. The direct D→DR comparison removes 1536 B in the first run and 1537 B in the repeat, with 110→108 objects in both. The repeat's candidate is 23616 B rather than 23617; the one-byte accounting difference is retained. Lifecycle allocation objects fall 119→117, and bytes 26737→25201.

The two added plain D allocations come from existing worker/join buffer growth, not an emitter-owned heap object. Original logical capacity 496 rounds to 512 B; the reservation changes it to 624, rounding to 640 B for each of the two buffers. This avoids two later 896 B growth allocations. DR requests 128 logical bytes per qualifying small function, at most 1024 per module. That logical cap is not a cap on total physical bytes: worker/join buffers, allocation rounding and the large serial-heap adjustment also matter. DR is limited to one worker, deferred mapping and effective noncompact compilation; implicit memory-pressure callbacks disable it.

No compilation-time reduction is established. DR public compile is +0.002% in its first normal comparison (not significant) and +1.33% in the repeat (p=.027). The one-call lifecycle is +0.30%/+0.47%, both nonsignificant. Both costs remain visible.

All four time differences in each direct run are nonsignificant. Guest bytes are exactly equal. Allocation-object savings repeat; timing savings do not.

## Native code, frames and register pressure

Kernel bytes include the adapter. Corpus function bytes are a different measurement; they are not interchangeable. Baseline/experimental kernel frames remain 56/88/168 B at live-parameter pressure 0/4/12; the corpus sum frame stays 40 B. Admitted grouped loops add no operand spills/reloads. Existing ABI/local stack transfers still occur. B/E reject the eight-chain emitter at pressure 12 and use existing 4/4, so those compile rows measure fallback.

| Candidate | Low-pressure kernel B | Corpus sum B | Corpus module B | Operand spills / reloads |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4/4 | 347 | 312 | 472 | 0 / 0 |
| A8/4 | 367 | Not measured | Not measured | 0 / 0 |
| B8/8 | 390 | Not measured | Not measured | 0 / 0 |
| C2/2 | 327 | Not measured | Not measured | 0 / 0 |
| D16/4 | 410 | 375 | 535 | 0 / 0 |
| E16/8 | 433 | Not measured | Not measured | 0 / 0 |
| H | 467 | 432 | 592 | 0 / 0 |
| T64 | 462 | 427 | 587 | 0 / 0 |
| T128 | 465 | 430 | 590 | 0 / 0 |
| T256 | 465 | 430 | 590 | 0 / 0 |
| P | 435 | 400 | 560 | 0 / 0 |
| DR | 410 | 375 | 535 | 0 / 0 |
| PR | 435 | 400 | 560 | 0 / 0 |

D adds 63 B versus 4/4; H adds 57 B over D; T64 adds 52 B; P adds 25 B. P kernel sizes at pressure 0/4/12 are 435/482/602 B versus D 410/457/577. D=DR and P=PR native bytes are exact matches.

A full group has one memory add per element plus four control instructions: static group instruction counts are 8 for 4/4, 12 for A/B, 6 for C, and 20 for D/E. D keeps four dependency chains and reduces main-group branch frequency from once per 4 elements to once per 16. B/E add four zeroing and four combination operations, 23 extra native bytes over their four-chain counterparts, and stricter register admission. H uses the same four accumulators for its four-element tail. P's two-load tail has 7 instructions versus 8 for two scalar loads, but adds a parity test/branch and retains per-load address/count dependencies. Its 100 B main group/backedge is byte-identical to D. The conservative P latch budget is 480 B.

D's unaligned streaming gain falls from 5.01% to 2.19%; its aligned streaming gain is not significant in the repeat. There is no repeated 5% streaming gain.

At fixed factor 8, changing four→eight chains produces no significant gain in the four measured cache cases. At factor 16, four→eight chains gives unaligned 8192 **+4.70% (p<.001)** and unaligned 262144 **−1.37% (p=.004)**; aligned cases are nonsignificant. The extra chains do not earn a consistent overall benefit.

## Real coverage and all corpus controls

The existing recognition search covered 125 corpus workload records and 223466 function bodies; only synthetic `memory.wasm` function 1/export `sum` matched. A bounded pinned external search checked 21 Wasm-R3 modules, 9441146 bytes and 18442 function bodies with no canonical exact-shape match. It did not compile/execute the external modules, excludes files above 2 MiB and noncanonical encodings, and is not proof that no reduction exists. **No eligible real application was found.**

The separate sizing scan covers 121 checked-in Wasm files: 120 decoded and 1 explicit unsupported-EH exclusion (MicroPython). Fourteen modules request headroom; thirteen are false positives relative to exact reduction recognition. `seqtk-fastq-to-fasta` local function 5 requests 128 logical B, has zero exact sum admission and identical guest bytes across all five modes. Its large serial-heap path reduces the increment to about 96 requested B, absorbed by the observed allocation class. This does not test the worst false-positive allocation-class boundary.

Seven original negative controls and eight latest controls have equal native hashes across their measured modes. Timing changes in these controls are retained but are not attributed to sum emission.

That rules out attribution to a sum loop but does not remove the measured regression. Host-binary layout or another timing effect remains possible and unproved. No same-binary D→DR time row is significant. No disabled-control time row or allocation-count difference is significant; this is no detected regression, not equivalence.

Normal-build code inspection confirms the existing 58 B body-size loop is byte-identical and contains no reservation branch/call. The whole compile function is 18762 B with a 3360 B frame, unchanged in size; stack-slot/data addresses differ, so whole-function byte equality is not claimed.

## Input-size and compilation recovery limits

Original D first reaches the repeated 5% target at 128 aligned elements and 256 unaligned; those are measured sizes, not universal thresholds. At 2048 it saves 20.13%/18.85% aligned and 14.11%/14.32% unaligned. At 64 it instead costs 1.03%/1.17% aligned and 1.83%/2.33% unaligned. Gains are not monotonic with size or alignment.

Median-only public compile recovery for reused synthetic sum(512) is D 84–121 executions, H 95–141 and T64 111–184. The latest DR first run adds 0.5 ns compile median and saves 9.325 ns/call, giving arithmetic recovery 1 call; repeat adds 305 ns and saves 9.820 ns/call, giving 32 calls. P's single public run has −9 ns compile delta and 5.850 ns/call saving, yielding zero added median compile cost. These are arithmetic estimates, **not statistically established break-even points** or application profitability claims. No added-cost recovery exists where execution is slower.

## Method, raw evidence and reproducibility

CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 8845HS, 16 MiB L3; Go 1.27.1, Linux/AMD64. Every decisive row has at least 20 interleaved baseline/candidate pairs with alternating order, `GOMAXPROCS=1`, `taskset -c 2`, identical Wasm/data/settings/features, and no overlapping builds. Follow-up timing windows are 150 ms; mitigation windows 100 ms. Execution excludes compilation/setup and includes the native call boundary. Diagnostic/register-check tags are omitted from timing binaries. Pressure 0/4/12 cases cover correctness and compile behavior; enabled execution timing with additional live parameters remains unmeasured.

Boost remains on; desktop activity and powersave governor remain; SMT sibling CPU 3 is not isolated. Pinning is not isolation. All favorable and unfavorable samples are retained. Benchstat supplies unpaired significance; CSV/JSON retain paired ratios and medians. P-values are not adjusted for multiple comparisons. Repeated practical effects, not isolated small p-values, guide the recommendation.

Phase 2 has 353 comparison rows and phase 3 adds 218. Original sweeps, repeated input-size runs and fixed-factor chain comparisons remain. Run 1 A/B predates binary hash capture; its candidate hash was not saved before rebuild, so only the separate hashed repeat supports the recommendation. Every later set records binary identity. Initial selector, setup and unavailable-Claude attempts remain documented.

Without it, that control is explicitly omitted.

## Correctness, reviews and validation

Tests precede implementations. Native execution is compared with an independent byte-addressed oracle, unchanged optimized Wago and scalar Wago. Coverage includes counts 0–9, 15–17, 31–33, later 0–35, 63–66, 127–130, 255–258, 511–513, 8192 and 262144; all remainders; aligned/unaligned addresses; nonzero seeds and integer overflow; full sparse 4 GiB memory32 wrapping; large count/address overflow; bounds/OOB traps and metadata; observable memory and source preservation; live exit locals; register pressure; budget limits; cleanup and executed fallback. Candidate markers must confirm admission, so a silent fallback is not accepted as correctness evidence.

All seven latest configurations pass the native matrix, including full 4 GiB execution. DR/PR deferred code/entry equality, actual reserved-code execution, public allocation equality and pressure callbacks at 0/1/1024 pass. The paired-tail 479 B budget rejection and adequate-budget register-pressure rejection preserve bytes/ownership and execute the fallback.

Two independent read-only reviews inspect correctness and performance evidence. Confirmed ownership-coverage, boundary, effective compact-mode, callback, bridge, selector and accounting findings are addressed. Both final reviews have no blocking findings. Claude Code was attempted with read-only Opus but returned `Not logged in`; **no Claude review occurred**.

Passed: full ordinary/checked unit suites, full checked bench, all selected native matrices, legacy tagged AMD64 statistics (`WAGO_SHARED_SCALAR=0`), guard-page runtime/public API tests, lint/generated checks, docs, tagged vet, shellcheck, shell/Python syntax and checked ARM64 cross-build. [Check status](https://github.com/wago-org/wago/blob/6a06dbe1d6ed603e36ed464071d09f7ed620e91e/experiments/specialized-sum-unroll/results/mitigation/check-status.txt).

The full normal shared-scalar statistics suite still has **exactly 86 baseline failure names, with no new failures**; [matched failure comparison](https://github.com/wago-org/wago/blob/6a06dbe1d6ed603e36ed464071d09f7ed620e91e/experiments/specialized-sum-unroll/results/mitigation/baseline-failure-comparison.json). ARM64 is cross-built, not executed. Full native OS/architecture, race/fuzz and conformance CI matrices are skipped under draft policy. Hardware counters, another CPU, controlled host code layout, positive eligible application gains and extra-live-parameter execution timing remain unvalidated.

[Draft smoke and CI passed on evidence head 6a06dbe1d](https://github.com/wago-org/wago/actions/runs/37952804380).

[Final correctness review](https://github.com/wago-org/wago/blob/6a06dbe1d6ed603e36ed464071d09f7ed620e91e/experiments/specialized-sum-unroll/results/mitigation/correctness-final-review.txt) · [Final performance review](https://github.com/wago-org/wago/blob/6a06dbe1d6ed603e36ed464071d09f7ed620e91e/experiments/specialized-sum-unroll/results/mitigation/performance-final-review.txt).

## Recommendation and scope

Retain 16/4 as the simplest main-loop candidate and DR as the best allocation mitigation. There is no fastest configuration for every count/alignment. H can be faster on some cache/remainder workloads, but grows code and has a direct unaligned-cache loss. The runtime gate lacks real-workload justification. More accumulators do not produce a consistent useful advantage. P fails short-loop recovery and the independent direct repeat.

**Investigate further; promote no default.** Real-application evidence remains absent, streaming benefits are inconsistent, short-loop losses remain, the latest public compile repeat costs 1.33%, and a negative control repeats a small loss. Retain all opt-in implementations and evidence for human review. Stop the bounded tuning study here.

Work remains in PR #910 and its existing worktree/branch. PR #909 is unchanged. No production default, public optimization option, ARM64 emitter, new worktree, additional PR, rebase, ready-for-review transition or merge is included.

Recorded-only follow-ups: direct 128-bit `i32`/`f32` SIMD map emission without module cloning/rewritten-Wasm allocations, retaining CPU profitability checks; and broader reduction recognition only when real coverage and measurements justify it.

Implementation/evidence lineage: original tests `ec0f965ea` and emitter `052b248bb`; follow-up tests `5bbee26aa`, hybrid `a07ce1e29`, threshold tests `d8104c5a2`, gates `0696004df`, validation/bridge `1a4c6e1ea`, hash audit `cb57571d5`, evidence `975247c4a`; mitigation tests `7cb15e21d`, paired tail `2540e0c38`, reservation `b21f51545`, selector correction `38eff78fb`, final evidence `6a06dbe1d`.

Evidence head: `6a06dbe1d6ed603e36ed464071d09f7ed620e91e`.
